patients.summary: Thirty-three-year-old teacher who joined in August 2023 and within months was found to have autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency, followed in 2025 by primary ovarian insufficiency and a single gout flare. An under-replacement ED visit in March 2026 led endocrinology to raise her fludrocortisone; outside letters arrive late or not at all.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to transfer her primary care here; her previous office is closing its adult panel. Teacher, wants something before school starts. Booked new-patient visit 8/23 at 1:00. Insurance card photo received through the portal. Records release form emailed for her old office to sign off on.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30F here to establish. Teaches second grade, married, no kids. Previous PCP office closed adult panel; records requested.

No chronic medical problems. No meds, no supplements. No surgeries. NKDA.

She says she has been more worn out than usual since around June, which she chalks up to a rough end of the school year and a lot of summer travel with her husband. Sleeping fine. No fevers, no GI complaints. Periods regular, monthly.

Family: mother has an underactive thyroid from autoimmune thyroiditis. A maternal aunt has type 1 diabetes. Paternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: never smoked. Has never drunk alcohol. No drugs.

Exam: slim, well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin without rash. Mood bright.

A/P
1. Health maintenance. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screens, she agrees. Pap per old records, will confirm date when they arrive. Flu vaccine when it comes in.
2. Fatigue, mild. Likely situational; labs above should cover the basics. Let me know if it is not lifting once school is back in session.

Follow up yearly or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Amy, all of your blood work came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are all normal, and both screening tests were negative. Nothing to do here. Good luck with the start of the year.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 14 pages from her former primary care practice covering 2016 to 2023. Annual exams only, no chronic diagnoses, no prescriptions on file. Cervical cytology 2022: negative. Tdap given May 2021. HPV vaccine series documented as completed in her teens. Flu shots most years. Indexed to chart and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after school for flu vaccine. Screening questions negative, no egg or vaccine reactions. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, lot recorded. VIS given. Tolerated well, waited 15 min. She mentions she is still dragging; told her to bring it up with the doctor, offered an appointment and she will call back to set one up.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back because the tiredness never lifted. Now about five months of it. Down about 3 kg since August without trying; clothes are loose. Feels flat and teary, less patience with her class, but not hopeless and no thoughts of self-harm. Has been wanting salty food all the time, putting salt on everything. Husband pointed out that she looks tan even though it is November, including on her knuckles. Periods have been coming every three weeks or so for the last few months instead of monthly. No fever, cough, vomiting, diarrhea. Updated COVID shot at her pharmacy last month.

O: BP 102/68 (lower than August). Wt 57.0 kg. Thin. Skin noticeably darker over the knuckles and elbows. Thyroid normal size. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, nontender.
PHQ-9: 8.

A/P: Fatigue, weight loss, salt craving and new hyperpigmentation with soft BP. Worried about primary adrenal insufficiency, especially with her family's autoimmune history. Mood symptoms likely part of the same picture.
- BMP and cortisol, drawn at 8 AM tomorrow before school
- I will call with results as soon as they post
- If vomiting, fainting or unable to keep fluids down: go to the ED, do not wait for me
PHQ-9 to be repeated once we know more.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reached her during her lunch break. Na 131, K 5.3, morning cortisol 2.9. Together with the exam this is very suggestive of primary adrenal insufficiency. Explained what that means in plain terms. Spoke directly with the endocrine office; they will see her 12/6 and will draw ACTH and do the rest of the workup there. Strict ED precautions reviewed again: vomiting, fainting, confusion, severe belly pain. She understands and her husband has the number. Asked her to go easy over the holiday weekend.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/06/2023
Reason for referral: low morning cortisol, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia

Thank you for asking us to see this 30-year-old schoolteacher. For roughly half a year she has been exhausted and low in mood and has lost weight she did not intend to lose. Over the same period her cycles shortened to about 21 days. She craves salt and has watched her skin darken, including in places that never see sun.

No prior medical problems; on no medications before today. No known drug allergies. No surgery. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drug use.
Family history: mother with autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt with type 1 diabetes; paternal grandmother with rheumatoid arthritis.

Exam: BP 100/70, HR 88, weight 56.5 kg. Thin. Hyperpigmented creases over the knuckles, elbows and knees. Thyroid not palpable. Cardiopulmonary exam normal.

Labs today: sodium 130, potassium 5.5, chloride 95, bicarbonate 22, BUN 18, creatinine 0.9, fasting glucose 70. ACTH elevated with low cortisol. 21-hydroxylase antibodies (resulted 12/14): positive.

Impression: primary adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune.

Plan:
1. Hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 10 mg in the late afternoon.
2. Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily.
3. Hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg IM emergency kit; she and her husband were taught to use it.
4. Sick-day rules: double the oral dose for fever or significant illness, inject and go to the ED if vomiting or unable to keep pills down. Medical alert bracelet advised.
5. Recheck electrolytes with PCP in about six weeks. Return here in six months.

No known drug allergies.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Saw endocrine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Wanted to let you know the endocrinologist agreed it is my adrenal glands, autoimmune type. I'm on hydrocortisone twice a day and another pill called fludrocortisone, plus I have an emergency shot now. Already a little less wiped out. Do I need to see you or just them?

documents.title: RE: Saw endocrine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Really glad you got in and that you are starting to feel it. Both, for now: endocrinology steers the doses, and I'd like you back here in about six weeks for a blood check and to see how you are doing. We haven't received their note yet, so please bring your bottles. Keep the emergency kit with you at school.

conditions.label: Addison disease
conditions.note: autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency, 21-hydroxylase antibody positive

medications.sig: Take 1.5 tablets (15 mg) by mouth on waking and 1 tablet (10 mg) in the late afternoon
Inject 100 mg into the muscle once for adrenal emergency, then go to the emergency department

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up six weeks into treatment. Endocrine consult letter finally arrived last week (reviewed, scanned).

She feels like a different person. Energy back to maybe 80 percent, eating well, salt craving gone. Mood much better; PHQ-9 now 3. Takes 15 mg hydrocortisone when she gets up and 10 mg around 3:30 after dismissal, fludrocortisone in the morning. Has the injection kit in her school bag; school nurse has a copy of the instructions. Ordered a medical ID bracelet.

BP 108/70. Wt 58.5 kg, up 1.5. Skin still a little darker on the knuckles but fading.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune (dx 12/2023 by endocrinology). Added to problem list. Med list reconciled from her bottles: hydrocortisone 15/10, fludrocortisone 0.1, emergency hydrocortisone kit. Recheck BMP today. Reviewed when to double up and when to inject.
2. Low mood, resolved with treatment of the above.

Next: annual in the fall. Endocrine follow-up in June.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your sodium (137) and potassium (4.4) are both back in the normal range, which tells us the doses are right for now. Keep doing what you are doing.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request from her pharmacy for hydrocortisone 10 mg tablets, 75 per month. Original prescriber is endocrinology, but she is out of refills and their next opening is not until June. Per PCP, one 90-day fill sent with same directions. Pt notified by text.

documents.title: Endocrine follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an FYI that I had my six month check with endocrine yesterday. They said my labs looked good and to keep the same doses of everything. They took over the hydrocortisone refills again. Not sure if they send you anything!

documents.title: RE: Endocrine follow up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Amy. We have not received anything from them yet; we will watch for it. Enjoy the summer break.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Early slot before school.

Interval: adrenal insufficiency stable on hydrocortisone 15/10 and fludrocortisone 0.1. Saw endocrine in June, no changes. No ED visits, has not had to use the injection. Energy good.

New issue: no period since about April. Before that they had been coming close together, then just stopped. Not on any contraception and she and her husband would like to get pregnant; home tests negative. No change in diet or exercise. Some hot nights recently but she blames the classroom radiator.

ROS otherwise negative. PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: well. BP normal. Thyroid normal. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal. Skin pigmentation now barely noticeable.

A/P
1. Secondary amenorrhea, about 6 months. Urine hCG in office negative. TSH with today's labs. Referring to gynecology for evaluation, she would like to be seen there given the fertility question too.
2. Primary adrenal insufficiency: stable. CMP today.
3. Health maintenance: flu vaccine given. Pap due next year (last 2022). Up to date otherwise.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from your physical is normal, including thyroid and electrolytes. The gynecology referral is in; their office will reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Referral status
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient asked about the GYN referral. Called their office: first new-patient opening is January 27. Booked; she accepted and is on their cancellation list. Pt aware.

documents.title: Gynecology Office Note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGY NEW PATIENT NOTE
Date of visit: 01/27/2025
Referred by: primary care, for amenorrhea

31-year-old G0 with autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency, diagnosed by endocrinology in December 2023, on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. Her cycles were regular for years, then ran short in late 2023, and she has now gone nine months without a period. Nothing changed around that time: same routine, same weight, no new stress, no new medication, no heavy exercise or dieting. Over the last few months she has noticed occasional drenching nights and some dryness with intercourse. She and her husband use no contraception and have been hoping for a pregnancy without success.

PMH: as above. PSH: none. Allergies: none known.
Social: teacher; never smoker; does not drink.
Family: no relatives with early menopause. Her younger sister was diagnosed with autoimmune adrenal insufficiency this past fall.

Exam: BMI 23. Normal breast and hair development. No nipple discharge on expression. Visual fields full to confrontation. External genitalia normal; cervix normal in appearance; vaginal mucosa mildly pale. Bimanual unremarkable.

Urine pregnancy test in clinic negative. Serum FSH (resulted 1/29) elevated, estradiol low.

Assessment: primary ovarian insufficiency, very likely part of her autoimmune endocrine picture.

Plan:
- Estradiol 1 mg by mouth daily
- Medroxyprogesterone 10 mg by mouth on days 1 to 12 of every month for endometrial protection
- Discussed what this means for fertility: spontaneous conception is uncommon but not impossible; options including donor-egg treatment were reviewed in general terms. She will talk it over with her husband before deciding on anything further.
- Return in 6 months.

Gynecology

conditions.label: Primary ovarian insufficiency
conditions.note: per gynecology, per patient report; note not yet received

conditions.label: Gout
conditions.note: acute gouty arthritis, right first MTP

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily on days 1 through 12 of each month
Take 2 tablets now and 1 tablet one hour later, then 1 tablet twice daily until the flare settles

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning; worked her in after school.

Woke at 2 AM with a throbbing right big toe. By morning the joint was swollen and red and she could barely tolerate the sheet on it. Taught all day in a slipper. No injury, no prior episodes, no fever or chills. Had not taken extra hydrocortisone.

Also: saw gynecology Monday. Told she has premature ovarian failure; started estradiol 1 mg daily and medroxyprogesterone 10 mg for the first 12 days of the month. Brought both bottles. We have no note from them yet.

Exam: afebrile. Wt 62.6 kg. Right 1st MTP warm, swollen, erythematous, exquisitely tender; ankle and other joints normal. No skin break, no streaking.

A/P
1. Acute gouty arthritis, right first MTP, clinical diagnosis. Uric acid today 7.4. Unusual at her age; her new estrogen deficiency may have nudged the urate up. Colchicine 1.2 mg now, 0.6 mg an hour later, then 0.6 mg twice a day until settled. No NSAID while dehydration risk and steroids are in play. Will not start long-term urate lowering after one flare. If fever or worsening redness, needs same day recheck to look at the joint.
2. Primary ovarian insufficiency (gynecology 1/27). Added to list with her estradiol and medroxyprogesterone. Will request their note.
3. Adrenal insufficiency: stable, no dose change. Reminded to double the hydrocortisone if she gets febrile.

documents.title: Toe
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Toe is totally back to normal, wearing real shoes again. Stopped the colchicine on Monday. Thank you for squeezing me in!

documents.title: RE: Toe
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. If it ever flares again, message me the same day and we will treat it early and talk about whether anything longer term makes sense.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Gynecology visit note from 1/27 never came. Called their office and refaxed our request with the signed release. They will send once the note is signed.

documents.title: Refill routed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request came to us for estradiol 1 mg. Prescriber of record is gynecology. Called pt; she has her follow-up with them in July and only needs enough to bridge. PCP approved 30 days with no refills.

documents.title: Specialist check-ins
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update for my file: saw endocrine in June and gyn yesterday. No changes to any of my medications from either. Endo said my numbers were fine.

documents.title: RE: Specialist check-ins
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Noted in your chart, thank you. Neither office has sent us a note so far.

results.text: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, before first bell.

Doing well. Adrenal insufficiency steady on hydrocortisone 15 mg AM / 10 mg afternoon and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg; endocrinology June, unchanged. On estradiol 1 mg daily with medroxyprogesterone days 1 to 12; monthly withdrawal bleeds, night sweats gone. She and her husband are still deciding about fertility treatment and are in no rush. No further toe trouble since January. Younger sister doing well on similar treatment.

PHQ-2 0. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well, BMI about 23. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Breasts symmetric without masses. Speculum: normal cervix, Pap with HPV co-test collected. Skin with only faint residual darkening on the knuckles.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap/HPV sent. Flu vaccine today; plans updated COVID at the pharmacy. CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH.
2. Primary adrenal insufficiency: stable.
3. Primary ovarian insufficiency: on replacement per gynecology.
4. Gout: single episode Jan 2025, none since.
Return for a check in the new year, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap was normal and HPV was not detected, so the next one is not due for five years. Blood counts, chemistry, thyroid and cholesterol all normal.

documents.title: Emergency kit renewal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called; her hydrocortisone injection vial expires next month and endocrine has not answered their refill line in a week. PCP sent a new vial of hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg to her pharmacy, no change. Reminded her to keep the old one until the new one is in hand.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD (received by fax)
Visit: 03/28/2026

CC: increasingly tired, dizzy when standing.

HPI: 32-year-old woman with autoimmune adrenal insufficiency and premature ovarian insufficiency. Several weeks of growing fatigue. Each morning she feels faint as she gets out of bed. Salt cravings are back, and she has lost weight while eating normally. Taking hydrocortisone 15 mg mornings and 10 mg afternoons and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily as prescribed; no missed doses. Denies fever, cough, chest pain, vomiting, diarrhea or abdominal pain.

PMH: primary adrenal insufficiency; primary ovarian insufficiency; history of gout.
Meds: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, estradiol 1 mg daily, medroxyprogesterone 10 mg days 1-12, hydrocortisone injection kit.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: nonsmoker, no alcohol.
Family: mother thyroid autoimmunity; maternal aunt type 1 diabetes; paternal grandmother rheumatoid arthritis.

Exam: T 36.7 C. Supine BP 96/62, HR 84. Standing BP 80/54, HR 102. Tired but alert, oriented. Mucous membranes dry. Darkened palmar creases and patchy pigment on the buccal mucosa. Heart regular, tachycardic on standing, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No focal neuro deficit.

Results: Na 129, K 5.4, glucose 66.

ED course: 2 L normal saline IV. Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV. Juice and a meal for the low glucose. Reassessed at 15:30: no longer lightheaded on standing, eating, walking steadily.

Impression: primary adrenal insufficiency with inadequate replacement; orthostatic hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, mild hypoglycemia. No infection identified.

Disposition: home with husband. Double oral hydrocortisone for 3 days, then resume usual dose. Endocrinology within 1 week; primary care in the next few days. Return for vomiting, confusion or fainting; use the injection kit if unable to keep pills down.
Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ER Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I ended up in the ER Saturday morning. I'd been so dizzy getting out of bed for a couple weeks and finally almost passed out in the bathroom. They gave me fluids and IV hydrocortisone and sent me home on double doses for 3 days. They said to see you this week and endo. I'm taking today off. Can I get in?

documents.title: RE: ER Saturday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: So sorry, Amy. You're booked Wednesday 4/1 at 3:45 with the doctor. If the dizziness comes back or you start vomiting before then, use your shot and go back to the ED. Please call endocrine this morning for the soonest slot.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit 3/28 (ED record not yet received; history from patient and her discharge paperwork). Her January check here was cancelled and never rebooked.

She finished three days of doubled hydrocortisone yesterday and is back to 15/10 with fludrocortisone 0.1. Much less dizzy, still tired, appetite fine. Swears she has not missed doses. No fever, no GI illness preceding this.

BP 104/68 seated, no symptoms on standing. Wt 59.2 kg, down about 3 kg since fall. Pigment on palmar creases a bit more obvious than at the physical.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency with under-replacement, recent ED visit. Salt craving, orthostasis and the high potassium point toward the mineralocorticoid side. BMP today. Endocrine appointment 4/21 confirmed by her. Not changing doses myself in the meantime; reviewed doubling rules if symptoms return.
2. POI on HRT, no change.
Updated COVID shot from the pharmacy last October added to record.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium 133 and potassium 5.2: better than in the ED but not back to normal. I've sent these to endocrinology ahead of your visit on the 21st. Keep salting your food freely until then.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 04/21/2026

Seen after an ED visit on 3/28 for orthostatic symptoms with hyponatremia (129), hyperkalemia (5.4) and glucose 66 on hydrocortisone 15/10 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. Improved after IV hydrocortisone and saline. Outpatient BMP 4/1 with Na 133, K 5.2. Still has mild morning lightheadedness and craves salt.

Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Renin (resulted 4/24): plasma renin activity elevated, consistent with mineralocorticoid under-replacement.

Plan: increase fludrocortisone to 0.15 mg daily (1.5 of the 0.1 mg tablets). Hydrocortisone unchanged at 15 mg on waking and 10 mg mid-afternoon. Sick-day rules and injection reviewed again. BMP in 2 to 3 months via primary care; return here in 6 months.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Fludrocortisone fill question
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacist called: pt is asking for an early fludrocortisone fill. Endocrinology changed the directions on 4/21 to 1.5 tablets daily and the old supply ran short. Our list still shows 0.1 mg daily; no endo note received. Pharmacy has the new prescription from endo and will fill it. FYI to PCP; will update list at her next visit once the letter arrives.

medications.sig: Take 1.5 tablets (0.15 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer follow-up. Endocrinology letter from 4/21 received in June and reviewed: renin was high and fludrocortisone went up to 0.15 mg daily, hydrocortisone the same.

Since the change she feels back to her baseline. No morning dizziness for over a month, salt cravings gone, regained most of the weight. Finished the school year without missing days. Still on estradiol and the 12-day medroxyprogesterone; gyn visit this month.

BP 112/72. Wt 61.5 kg. Pigment fading again. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency: now on fludrocortisone 0.15 mg daily per endocrinology; med list updated. Hydrocortisone 15 mg AM / 10 mg PM unchanged. BMP today, as endo asked. Watch BP and for swelling on the higher dose.
2. POI on estradiol/medroxyprogesterone, followed by gynecology.
3. Gout: no recurrence.
Annual physical in October; flu shot then.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium 138 and potassium 4.3, both normal on the new fludrocortisone dose. I've copied endocrinology. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request for hydrocortisone 10 mg tabs, #75. Endocrine is prescriber but pt asked us to send a 90-day supply before the school year starts. PCP approved, same sig. Sent.
